about: Held-out sign-off cases the call-sign reader does not answer as a careful operator would (docs/callsigns.md, A call sign at the end). Written by a separate agent from the rule alone, to find what gets past it. `expect` is what the operator would want. Since a call sign at the end became a question for the operator [237], none of these names a unit by itself: the ones that wanted no sender get a question the operator turns down, and the real sign-offs the rule refuses wait in the tray, most with no suggestion. Not part of npm test.

cases.text: Push up to the station and hold the north entrance, Bravo 2.
cases.note: An order to BRAVO 2 with no 'you' and no tie word; the rule as written reads a sign-off.

cases.text: Go ahead, Alpha 1.
cases.note: The usual reply to a call: someone tells ALPHA 1 to send its message, and nothing was reported.

cases.text: Where is the drone now, Alpha 2.
cases.note: A question that speech-to-text wrote with a full stop, so rule 6 does not see it.

cases.text: Three units at the town hall now: Alpha 1, Charlie 3, Bravo 2.
cases.note: A list of three units seen; the last one comes after a comma and looks like a sign-off.

cases.text: Movement at the corner of the church, I think that's... Alpha 2.
cases.note: A hesitation written as dots, after 'that's', which is not on the tie-word list: the speaker names who they see.

cases.text: Je ne vous vois pas devant la mairie, avancez jusqu'à la gare, Bravo deux.
cases.note: French 'vous' and an order: it speaks to BRAVO 2, but 'vous' is not in rule 6.

cases.text: Рухайся до церкви і чекай на дрон, Соколе, прийом.
cases.note: The vocative case («Соколе») is how Ukrainian speaks to someone; it is never a sign-off.

cases.text: White van parked at the station, partial plate, two characters only, Charlie 3.
cases.note: A number plate spelled out: 'Charlie 3' is the letter C and the digit 3, not a unit.

cases.text: The bridge behind the château is blocked, we got that a minute ago, from Bravo 2.
cases.note: A relay: 'from' names where the news came from, not who is speaking, and the pause sits right before it.

cases.text: Two vehicles stopped at the crossroads east of the church, grid.
cases.note: The transmission was cut off before the grid numbers; 'grid' is one letter from 'Grim' and must not be a near match for ГРІМ.

cases.text: Team on the roof of the town hall is friendly, identified as. Bravo 2.
cases.note: Speech-to-text put a full stop in the middle of 'identified as Bravo 2'; 'as' is not on the tie-word list.

cases.text: Il y a une équipe devant la mairie avec un drone, c'est Bravo deux.
cases.note: French 'c'est' here means 'that is': the speaker says who the team is, not who is speaking.

cases.text: moving north on avenue de paris two hundred metres from the station alpha one out
cases.note: A real sign-off with no punctuation at all, as speech-to-text sometimes writes; rule 4 refuses it.

cases.text: Two vehicles at the church heading north - Bravo 2.
cases.note: The pause is written as a hyphen with spaces around it, which speech-to-text uses for a dash.

cases.text: At the château, north gate is open, one vehicle inside, will send the grid when we have it, Charlie 3, wait out.
cases.note: A real sign-off followed by 'wait out', which is not on the closing-word list.

cases.text: Drone is back at the château, battery at 20 percent, landing now, Alpha 1. Thank you for watching.
cases.note: Speech-to-text often writes 'Thank you for watching' for silence; only 'thank you' is a closing word.

cases.text: At the church now, in position, Alpha Two, over.
cases.note: 'in position' ends the report and 'position' is a tie word, so rule 5 refuses a real sign-off.

cases.text: Base, be advised the vehicle you asked about is at the château, north gate, Charlie 3.
cases.note: The 'you' is the command post, named at the start; rule 6 refuses a real sign-off.

cases.text: Control, can we get the drone over the church? Two vehicles there now. Alpha 2, over.
cases.note: A unit asks the command post a question and then signs off; the earlier question mark makes rule 6 refuse it.

cases.text: Bravo 2, I'm at the station, nothing moving on Avenue de Paris. Do you copy, Base?
cases.note: The unit speaks to the command post by name at the end; the new command-post rule reads it as the command post speaking.
